purpose: Vinorelbine is a chemotherapy medicine used mainly to treat non-small cell lung cancer. It may also be used for breast cancer and some other types of cancer. Your doctor has prescribed it as part of your cancer treatment plan.
how_it_works: Cancer cells grow and divide very quickly. Vinorelbine works by blocking the machinery inside cancer cells that they need to split and multiply. By interfering with this process, the medicine helps stop cancer cells from growing and spreading. Healthy cells can also be affected, which is why some side effects occur.
common_side_effects: Low white blood cell count (which raises your infection risk), fatigue and weakness, nausea and vomiting, constipation, numbness or tingling in hands and feet, hair thinning or loss, mouth sores, and loss of appetite. Pain, redness, or irritation at the injection site is also common if given by vein.
warnings: This medicine can seriously lower your blood cell counts, making it easier to get infections, bleed, or feel very tired — your blood will be checked regularly. Tell your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, unusual bruising or bleeding, or signs of infection. Vinorelbine can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable contraception during treatment. Avoid it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It can cause nerve damage over time, so report any new numbness, tingling, or muscle weakness promptly.
typical_dosing: Vinorelbine is usually given once a week as an injection into a vein (IV) in a clinic or hospital, or sometimes taken as a capsule by mouth on a weekly schedule. The exact dose depends on your body size, overall health, and how well your body tolerates the medicine. Your oncology team will determine the right dose and schedule for you.
